samples.report:
**MEMORANDUM — FLXS / Flexsteel Industries, Inc.** (pack rev 21; T0 $88.82 as of 2026-10-02)

The desk is now closed (2/2 runs). The final run — answer-run inputs unchanged plus a verified crux — returned identical scenario values to the prior complete run, so desk parity holds throughout: **Base $72.50 / Bull $86.86 / Bear $42.05**.

---

## SECTION 0 — Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | FLXS / Flexsteel Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ) — US residential furniture manufacturer/importer [Actual] |
| Price T0 | $88.82 [Actual, vendor quote 2026-10-02]; market cap $361M; at 52-week high (range 34.0–90.65) |
| **Verdict** | **OVERVALUED** — crux-verified (desk `crux_check`: both inputs "reachable", all four PRIMARY P1 quotes found). Base $72.50 = 82% of price; probability-weighted $68.48 = −22.9% vs T0 |
| Base / Bull / Bear (final desk run) | **$72.50 / $86.86 / $42.05** [Estimate — desk] |
| Probabilities | 50% / 25% / 25% → expected IV **$68.48**, expected return **−22.9%** [Estimate — desk] |
| Margin of safety | Base −18.4%; Bull −2.2% (Bull below price); Bear −52.7% [Estimate — desk] |
| Kelly | Full 0.00%, quarter-Kelly **0.00% — NO_ALLOCATION**; payoff skew −0.04x [Estimate — desk] |
| Neutral reverse DCF | Price implies **+3.26% 10-yr cash-flow CAGR** — below the <p50 median (8.9%) for this size bucket; own-assumption structure implies stage-1 growth +9.53% vs −0.8% demonstrated 5-yr CAGR → **expectations gap +10.3 pts, flagged HIGH by the desk** [Estimate — desk] |

The stock is up +151.6% over 12-1 months and +61.7% over 6 months, at its 52-week high, sector-neutral momentum z +3.0 [Actual, DATA 2.5]. The August spike was triggered by a record GAAP EPS print ($6.07) that included a one-time $9.0M IEEPA tariff refund (780 bps of Q4 margin) [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Ex-refund adjusted operating margin *fell* from 9.0% to 7.1% [Actual, PRIMARY P1], and the company's own Q1 FY27 guide embeds further compression to 6.5–7% GAAP operating margin [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Every sell-side target ($79–80) sits below the price [Estimate, DATA 8].

---

## SECTION 1 — Macro (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates/regime:** rf 10y 5.24%, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36%; CPI 3.35% / PCE 3.42% YoY; curve +0.45% steepening; regime vector goldilocks 0.341 / reflation 0.271 / tightening 0.176 — contested (margin 0.070) [Actual, DATA 1.5]. Markets are pricing possible further hikes on persistent inflation (DATA 1.6, 2026-09-25).
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock`, severity 1, direction up, onset 2026-09-28 — Strait of Hormuz closure unresolved, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Russia sanctions [Actual, DATA 1.6]. This is the single most important macro fact for FLXS: the company's own release names "logistics and material cost inflation driven by elevated energy prices" as the key variability driver of its outlook [Actual, PRIMARY P1, 2026-08-17].
- **Exposure:** Flexsteel manufactures in the US and Mexico (long-lived assets $40.3M US / $31.4M MX) [Actual, PRIMARY P2] — freight, fuel, foam/wood/resin inputs and peso translation (a 100 bps Q4 FX headwind was already booked [Actual, P1]) all transmit the oil shock into COGS. Demand side: furniture is an affordability-sensitive discretionary purchase; management cites "weak confidence, affordability constraints" [Actual, P1]. A 5.24% 10y also suppresses housing turnover, the upstream driver of case-goods demand.
- **COE anchor:** 10.04% = rf_eff 5.24% + 1.149× loading × 4.17% premium [Actual, DATA 1.5]. Used unchanged for Base/Bull; Bear carries a +150 bps credit-shock (mandate 4) to 11.54%.

---

## SECTION 2 — Business and Moat

**Economic engines (mandate 1):**
1. **Transactional deliveries — ~100% of the business.** Single operating segment: design, manufacture and import of residential furniture (soft seating, case goods; exited the ~$12M Homestyles RTA line in FY26) [Actual, P1/P2]. FY26 growth was price-led: pricing +10–11% masked unit-volume declines [Unconfirmed — press coverage; direction consistent with P1's volume commentary]. A commodity-cyclical engine: no contracted backlog >1x revenue, no multi-year visibility.
2. **Captive installed base / annuity — none.** Furniture has no service annuity, no recurring contractual revenue, no fleet. Backlog of ~$79.5M ≈ 0.17x annual revenue [Unconfirmed — catalyst brief 2026-04-21; the Q3 release mirrors I read do not print an orders line]. **No annuity is credited in any scenario.**
3. **Strategic optionality — small but real:** health & wellness category, strategic account relationships, consumer-insights/AI capability build (new digitally-experienced independent director, effective 2026-09-10 [Actual, P3]), Mexico cost arbitrage, and a management-stated ≥8% long-term adjusted operating margin target vs 7.5% in FY26 [Unconfirmed — Lytham conference coverage, 2026-10-05; consistent with the strategy language in P1].

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** Base = normalized FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) owner cash flow: adjusted operating income $34.45M (GAAP $42.55M less one-time IEEPA tariff refund $9.01M and Homestyles exit costs $0.91M, per the P1 reconciliation [Actual]) × (1 − 23% Q4 effective rate) + D&A $3.83M − capex $3.94M − SBC $4.55M = **$21.9M** [Estimate — my normalization of filed figures]. SBC is treated as a real cost, deducted once in cash flow (sbc_treatment = deducted_in_cf); the basic share count is therefore used. Capex is only ~0.9% of sales — a genuinely asset-light replacement cycle.

**Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3):** scale/dual-country footprint 2; brand (recognized but no demonstrated pricing power beyond surcharges) 1; IP (patented Blue Steel Spring [Unconfirmed — research brief only, not in filings]) 1; network effects 0; channel/strategic accounts 1; switching costs/installed base 0; execution & cost discipline 2. **Total 7/21 → moat 2.3/5.0 (narrow), direction stable-to-improving** on execution, structurally unchanged.

**Financial strength:** No bank debt — $16.7M cash, ~$54.1M undrawn secured line [Actual, P1]; the $52M "total debt" in DATA 6 is operating-lease liabilities (DATA 6C), not interest-bearing debt (FY26 interest expense $22K [Actual, P1]). FY26: OCF $51.5M, FCF ~$47.6M ("more than $47.5 million" [Actual, P1]); $63.7M of buybacks funded in-year [Actual, P1]; dividend +25%. Piotroski 7/8; accruals −0.069 (earnings are cash-backed); net share count −3.9%/yr [Actual, DATA 7]. The balance sheet is the strongest part of this business.

---

## SECTION 3 — Valuation

**Desk inputs (all passed to run_financial_model; equity frame because every pack flow is after-interest):**

| Input | Value | Default? | Reason for departure |
|---|---|---|---|
| base_cf | $21.9M FY26 normalized owner CF [Estimate] | default not available (no TTM/D&A in DATA 3) | Built from P1 filed figures: adj. op income ex one-time refund + D&A − capex − SBC; excludes the $9.0M one-time IEEPA refund that flattered FY26 |
| Base growth y1–y5 | +3%, +10%, +4.6%, +4.0%, +3% [Assumption] | no consensus CF level in DEFAULTS (reference_status not_available) | y1 anchored to the company's Q1 FY27 guide (sales +1–4%, GAAP margin 6.5–7% vs 7.5% FY26 adj — compression, PRIMARY P1 2026-08-17); y2 = margin recovery toward the 8% target as energy costs stabilize; y3–y5 at/below next-FY consensus revenue growth +4.6% (DATA 8) |
| Fade | 4 years | — | Fades from last explicit rate to terminal g over the reinvestment/productivity runway |
| terminal_g | 2.64% | = default | Own 8-yr revenue trend, held between breakeven inflation and anchor |
